scope: Primary literature on statement-preserving Lean proof refactoring and the review's reproduction repository.

references.title: ProofOptimizer: Training Language Models to Simplify Proofs without Human Demonstrations
references.claim_supported: Reports shortening generated Lean proofs while checking replacements against the original statements. Section 2 defines token length; Section 5.2 and Appendix H distinguish source length from execution cost. These experiments do not evaluate the six OpenAI developments in this review.

references.title: Lean Refactor: Multi-Objective Controllable Proof Optimization via Agentic Strategy Search
references.claim_supported: Studies length, compilation cost, and cross-version compatibility as distinct Lean refactoring objectives, including competition and research repositories. Its experiments do not establish redundancy in this review's six case studies.

references.title: Proof Architecture in the OpenAI Lean Library: manuscript, data, and reproduction code
references.claim_supported: Manuscript source, retained corpus data and source hashes, analysis scripts, original Lean examples, and verification records. Release v1.6.1 identifies the accompanying reproduction edition.

deferred_reference.author: Shiva Kintali
deferred_reference.title: A Short Proof of the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis
deferred_reference.decision: Excluded from manuscript supporting evidence at the user's request: newly released, unreviewed proposal whose mathematical correctness has not been assessed. It supplies no Lean formalization and changes the quantitative conclusion.
